Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

  MONDAY, FEBRUARY 17, 2026

The City Council of the City of Azusa met in Closed and Regular session at Azusa Auditorium at 213 E.
Foothill Blvd., Azusa, CA 91702.

Mayor Alvarez called the meeting to order at 6:30 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BOW

of Police Wenrick, Police Captain Landeros, Director of Administrative Services Johnson, Director of

 Economic & Community Development Jimenez, Director of Public Works Delgadillo, Director of Community

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Captain Landeros.

The Invocation was led by Reverend Dr. Kristina Collins, Sanctuary for Spiritual Living.

City Attorney Richman reported that one item was discussed during Closed Session, with no reportable action.

CEREMONIAL

Swearing in of Azusa Police Department Officers and Presentation of Non-Sworn Staff.

Police Chief Wenrick introduced the non-sworn staff to the City Council.

City Clerk Cornejo administered the Oath of Office to the following non-sworn staff:

Administrative Services Manager Tachias; Executive Assistant Julissa Ramirez; Dispatch Supervisor
Santamaria; Records Supervisor Valenzuela; SSO Rios; SSO Tinoco; SSO Plantillas; SSO Sanchez; SSO

Police Chief Wenrick introduced the sworn Police Officers to the City Council.

City Clerk Cornejo administered the Oath of Office to the following sworn personnel:

Corporal Saenz; Corporal Corona; Corporal Avalos; Corporal Aguirre; Corporal Gomez; Corporal Hildebrandt;
Corporal Wold; Corporal Shepard; Sergeant Johnson; Sergeant Beaver; Sergeant Martinez; Sergeant Munoz;
Lieutenant Chapman; Lieutenant Vasconcellos; Lieutenant Sears; Officer Wyman; Officer Cheng; Officer
Reynolds; Officer Sera; Officer Gutierrez; Officer Torres; Officer Castro; Officer Bentz; Officer Bernal; and
Officer Jimenez.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

Tomas Torices, Yaneth Rodriguez, Koy Parada, Dr. Catherine Heinlein, and Sandra Perez spoke in support of
Item C-2 (Tobacco Control); thanked the Council for considering a tobacco retail license and expressed
appreciation for the City’s commitment to providing residents with transparent information regarding the public
health impacts of tobacco and nicotine use; and also encouraged the Council to consider adopting tobacco
control polices.

REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

‘Pet of the Month’ Presentation by Los Angeles County Animal Care & Control.

Officer Wesley from Los Angeles County Animal Care and Control introduced Tommy, a six-month-old male
orange and white tabby.

Presentation: Los Angeles General Medical Center Foundation.

Dr. Julia Ruedas gave a presentation to the City Council regarding efforts to reduce youth access to tobacco
products; explained that youth currently have significant access to these harmful products, which puts their
health and future at risk; noted that adopting a Tobacco Retail License (TRL) policy has proven effective in
reducing youth access to tobacco products and lowering rates of cigarette and e-cigarette use among youth and
young adults.

She further stated that 26 local cities have adopted similar policies; shared that community surveys were
conducted in Azusa, with 85% of respondents indicating that their community has been negatively impacted by
smoking and tobacco use; and encouraged the Council to consider taking the next steps to move the Azusa

City Council Minutes  Page | 2
February 17, 2026
 community forward in partnership with the Breathe Clean Coalition.
The Council inquired about the data collection methods used in the surveys to which Dr. Ruedas explained that
trained Staff conducted outreach by visiting stores and engaging with residents to gather information.

The Council noted that a TRL policy is not currently in place and emphasized the importance of taking the next
steps to address tobacco regulation and discussed the existing tobacco ordinance. The Council inquired whether
it could be strengthened, potentially incorporating TRL components, rather than creating an entirely new policy.
Staff were directed to research these options and return with recommendations.

City Manager Communications

None.

Councilmember Announcements

Mayor Pro Tem Avila announced that an e-waste drop-off event will take place on February 21 at the Azusa
Public Works Yard and Family Bingo Night will take place on February 24 at the Azusa Library; congratulated
a new business, B-Flow Pilates, on its ribbon-cutting ceremony; thanked everyone who attended the Casino
Night event and requested certificates be presented to the organizations that received proceeds from the event
at the following Council meeting; and extended appreciation to the event sponsors, including Athens,
Transtech, and Azusa Connects.

Councilmember Mendez announced upcoming events at the Azusa Library, including Toddler Story Time on
February 19 and Family Craft Hour featuring Balloon Abstract Art on March 3; congratulated Mayor Pro Tem
Avila and Councilmember Gonzales on the success of Casino Night and thanked them for their efforts in
protecting and promoting Azusa youth sports; and congratulated the Azusa High School Varsity Boys
Basketball Team for winning the league championship—their first since 1974—and requested that the team be
recognized with certificates at a future Council meeting.

Councilmember Bow announced Little Learners Playtime scheduled for February 25 at the Azusa Library;
noted that the City will commemorate the Lunar New Year during its 3rd Annual Celebration on February 28 at
Memorial Park; and extended well wishes to the community for a happy Lunar New Year.

Councilmember Gonzales announced Family Storytime with the local fire station on March 4, followed by
Toddler Story Time on March 5 at the Azusa City Library; reported attending a conference in Sacramento
related to AB 1234; and requested a certificate in recognition of the 10-year anniversary of Encouragement
Church.

Mayor Alvarez announced free after-school tutoring at the Azusa City Library on Mondays and Tuesdays;
reported attending the ribbon cutting for B-Flow Pilates and shared that Panera Bread is scheduled to open in
Azusa on February 20.

SCHEDULED ITEMS

CONSIDERATION AND FIRST READING OF AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
CITY OF AZUSA CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 2 (ADMINISTRATION), CHAPTER 14
(BUILDINGS AND BUILDING REGULATIONS), CHAPTER 18 (BUSINESSES), CHAPTER 46
(OFFENSES AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS), CHAPTER 58 (SOLID WASTE), AND
CHAPTER 70 (TAXATION) OF THE AZUSA MUNICIPAL CODE (“AMC”) RELATING TO THE
BOARD OF APPEALS, EMERGENCY ACCESS SYSTEMS, NUISANCES, GRAFFITI ABATEMENT,
REAL PROPERTY RECORDS REPORT, RESIDENTIAL RENTAL REGISTRATION AND
INSPECTION, REGISTRATION AND MAINTENANCE OF VACANT PROPERTIES,
SCAVENGING, PROHIBITED TYPES OF DISPOSAL, AND SHORT-TERM RENTALS

Community Improvement Manager Edson provided the Council with proposed code amendments; explained
that the amendments would address the Board of Appeals, emergency access systems, real property records
reports, the Residential Rental Registration Program, the Vacant Property Registration Program, collection and
donation bins, and short-term rentals; presented staff recommendations and made himself available to answer
questions.

Edson responded to questions regarding the amended ordinance, explaining that when a boarded-up property is
identified, the new amendment allows staff to initiate the vacant property registration process. If property

City Council Minutes  Page | 3
February 17, 2026
 owners fail to comply, enforcement actions may include citations and further abatement measures.

He clarified that the section regarding real property reports remains largely unchanged, with only adjustments
made to reporting dates; and discussed updates to the illegal dumping section, noting that the City now has the
authority to charge offenders with a misdemeanor and impose fines of up to $1,000 if they are caught dumping
illegally; mentioned that the department is now fully staffed and that team members are being trained to take a
more proactive approach; and Staff are also meeting with apartment complexes to educate property
management and tenants on proper disposal methods for bulky items.

Moved by Councilmember and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Avila and carried by unanimous vote of the
Council to Introduce an Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Azusa, California, amending Chapter 2
(Administration), Chapter 14 (Buildings and Building Regulations), Chapter 18 (Businesses), Chapter 46
(Offenses and Miscellaneous Provisions), Chapter 58 (Solid Waste), and Chapter 70 (Taxation) of the Azusa
Municipal Code (“AMC”) relating to the Board of Appeals, emergency access systems, nuisances, graffiti
abatement, real property records report, residential rental registration and inspection, registration and
maintenance of vacant properties, scavenging, prohibited types of disposal, and short-term rentals; and
Determine that the adoption of this Resolution does not qualify as a “project” as defined in California
Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code Section 21000 et seq.) (“CEQA”). Section 15378.

Economic and Community Development Director Jimenez delivered a brief presentation regarding a
professional services agreement with Raimi + Associates; informed the Council that Staff was recently notified
that Raimi + Associates has been consolidated with Alta Planning + Design.; and explained that Council
approval is required to assign the existing agreement from Raimi + Associates to Alta Planning + Design.

He noted that there are no changes to the principals involved and that the transition is primarily a structural
adjustment. He also addressed how the agreement aligns with the City’s General Plan objectives.

Moved by Councilmember Mendez and seconded by Councilmember Gonzales and carried by unanimous vote
of the Council to: Consider and approve the assignment of the existing Professional Services Agreement for
General Plan and Zoning Code update services from Raimi + Associates to Alta Planning + Design; Receive
and file a status update on the ongoing General Plan and Zoning Code update efforts, and provide direction
regarding the identification and engagement of external stakeholders; and Determine that the Assignment of the
PSA does not constitute a “project” under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), as defined in
Public Resources Code Section 21000 et seq. (Section 15378).
